title: SessionClient 'Clone is cheap' doc-claim depends on un-asserted upstream JmapClient invariant
description:
src/methods/mod.rs:117-119 — SessionClient's doc-comment claims:

    Clone is derived because JmapClient is itself cheap-to-clone (it
    already implements Clone and with_metadata_session clones one
    internally), enabling parallel-task fan-out with one bound session.

The 'cheap-to-clone' claim about JmapClient is a contract assertion this crate cannot enforce — JmapClient lives in jmap-base-client. If a future jmap-base-client revision makes Clone expensive (e.g. deep-clone of an internal config map, or a new field that requires deep duplication), this crate's doc-comment becomes a lie and downstream callers fan-out tasks under a false performance assumption.

Two reinforcing mitigations:
(a) Add a compile-time-asserted bound — e.g. assert in a #[test] that 'JmapClient: Clone' holds (already true; this just freezes it).
(b) Document the dependency-on-upstream-invariant explicitly: 'Clone is derived; cheap-clone is contingent on jmap_base_client::JmapClient::clone remaining cheap. See jmap-base-client docs for that contract.'

Recommendation: (b). Cheap doc edit. Tells the caller where the 'cheap' guarantee actually lives so they can verify upstream.

Workspace-wide: same claim appears in canonical mail-client SessionClient doc-comment. Propagate.

Borderline opinion — could argue this is just careful prose and not a real engineering concern. But the contract claim is technically unenforceable from this crate, so a defensive doc update is justified. Leaving at P4 and unlabelled-opinion to mark 'file but low priority'.
close_reason: Triage 2026-10-31 at c07d5206: moot: metadata-client SessionClient and its Clone-is-cheap doc deleted in c4496114 (crate-jmap-metadata-client/src/lib.rs:14-36)
